thread:
mike_customer: Quick heads-up, after the midnight rollout a few customers report weird extra text appended to otherwise short deterministic outputs. Example below.

mike_customer: curl example we used (non-streaming):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v2","input":"Summarize: 'Status OK'","max_tokens":12}'
```

mike_customer: expected: "Status: OK"
mike_customer: observed: "Status: OK. Let me know if you need anything else." — looks like leftover assistant turn from a previous session.

tara_support: thanks for reporting @mike_customer. Can you tell us: org id, route, whether you use session ids, and whether this is hosted or dedicated? Also include a raw response with headers if possible.

mike_customer: org=org-7721 route=quick-summary hosted session_id not used. Raw response (sensitive fields redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rrw-cache-hit: yes
x-rrw-cache-key: prefix:org-7721:route-quick-summary:kv_default
x-rrw-model: redwood-embed-v2
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"res_abc","output":"Status: OK. Let me know if you need anything else."}
```

lee_runtime: hm cache-hit with prefix key — does the route use any system prompt or implicit assistant initialization? If the prefix cache key doesn't include a model artifact id, old KV could be applied to new model.

yana_eng: we did a minor compile tweak between v2 and v2.1 (tokenizer normalization and an optimized attention kernel). If the cache namespace stayed identical, entries produced pre-rollout might be reused.

lee_runtime: I tried to reproduce on staging. With the existing prefix cache I consistently get the appended sentence. If I purge prefix entries for the route it returns the tight expected text. Small staging log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-26T01:17:03Z] cache.lookup key=prefix:org-7721:route-quick-summary:kv_default -> HIT
[2026-03-26T01:17:03Z] kv.apply returned 64 tokens of prefix (sessionless)
[2026-03-26T01:17:03Z] model=redwood-embed-v2.1 kernel=attn-opt
```

lee_runtime: that 64 tokens from previous invocation is the extra text. The cache key lacks a model_compile_id.

tara_support: short-term mitigation options for customers?

mike_customer: rolling back isn't an option for us. We need either a flush or a header to opt out of cache reuse.

lee_runtime: two immediate fixes we can apply: 
1) We can flush the prefix cache for the route from infra. Endpoint (internal):
```
POST /internal/clear_prefix_cache
Body: {"org":"org-7721","route":"quick-summary"}
```
2) Client-side temporary change: include header `x-rrw-kv-bypass: 1` to skip prefix reuse, or send `kv_namespace` param including `model_compile_id` to avoid hitting legacy entries.

yana_eng: I've drafted a mitigation patch to include `model_compile_id` in prefix KV keys so cache entries are scoped to an exact model artifact. Opening PR with unit tests that change tokenization semantics and assert cache miss on model bump.

ci_bot: CI job #bk-20260326-54 started for branch patch/add-model-id-to-kv-key

jo_sre: note: flushing will induce cold prefix rebuilds and a small latency spike for the first N requests; we'll coordinate timing with the customer for low traffic.

mike_customer: please go ahead and flush now; we'll also flip the bypass header on our side for the next 30 minutes.

ci_bot: CI job #bk-20260326-54 passed -> ready to merge.

jo_sre: clear_prefix_cache call executed: 
```
[2026-03-26T01:35:10Z] clear_prefix_cache org=org-7721 route=quick-summary removed=9 entries result=ok
[2026-03-26T01:35:10Z] next_requests -> cache_miss -> regenerate_prefix
```

lee_runtime: after flush confirmed, same request returns: 
```
{"id":"res_def","output":"Status: OK"}
```

mike_customer: verified on our side as well. output is clean. thanks.

yana_eng: long-term plan: land the PR that binds KV keys to compile-time model digest, add server-side automatic invalidation on any model deployment that changes compile id, and add a migration to mark legacy KV entries so operators can selectively evict.

ci_bot: PR merged to release-hotfix. Deploy pipeline triggered to canary.

lee_runtime: followups for support: 1) notify affected customers that flush completed and explain root cause (stale prefix KV after model compile change), 2) suggest `x-rrw-kv-bypass` as temporary guard, 3) ask customers to report if they still see anomalies in 24 hours.

tara_support: I'll send updates to the incident list and create a postmortem note describing detection (alerts on cache_hit && unexpected_output) and remediation steps.

mike_customer: closing once we confirm 24h clean. thanks for quick action. :rocket:
